To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel variant in the DNA mismatch repair (MMR) gene MLH1 is associated with susceptibility for colorectal cancer (the most common cancer type worldwide), and this variant is found in both Jews and Arabs in Israel.

we identified a novel MLH1 missense mutation, 415C, in 1.3% (5/386) of Jewish, Christian and Islamic individuals with CRC in Israel and that this mutation is associated with a high risk of sporadic CRC.

we identified a new MLHP1 variant, MLH1 132D→H, that is associated with microsatellite-stability sporadic colorectal cancers, and that this variant confers a higher risk of CRC than does the classic HNPCC mutation MLH1 936G→A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic susceptibility to colorectal carcinoma, a common and potentially lethal malignancy.
the identification of novel genetic variants that confer increased susceptibility to sporadic cancer.
the role of the MLH1 D134H variant in susceptibility to sporadic and familial CRC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new MLH1 D 132H variant confers a significant risk of sporadic CRC and that it is a novel mechanism in microsatellitestable tumors.
MLH1 132H is associated with susceptibility in sporadic CRC.
the MLH1 variant 415C is associated with a high risk of sporadic microsatellitemutable CRC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the D132H variant of MLH1 confers a high-risk for CRC and identifies a new mechanism in microsatellitestable tumors.
the MLH1 D133H mutation is a new, high-penetrant mutation in MLH1 associated with microsatellite-stability CRC.
MLH1 132H is a new, high-risk variant for CRC that is associated with a microsatellite-stability phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MLH1 D133H variant is associated to a higher risk of sporadic CRC, and that the risk is not associated with MSI.
the D132H mutation in MLH1 is associated with susceptibility for sporadic microsatelite stable colorectal cancer (MSSCRC).
there are many different mechanisms by which people can be at risk for cancer, and that the mechanisms that cause cancer can be quite different from one person to another.
